workflows.title: Let me draw you a picture...
workflows.description: This is a 2-hour in-class activity in a Visual Communication course. Students choose a subject to diagram that they have expert knowledge of. They are free to choose any graphic media, but are restricted to an 11x17 maximum format. By eliminating the performance stress of communicating something outside their expertise and allowing them to choose their favourite drawing tools, students are naturally confident and engaged in the activity. Under the guise of play, the exercise incorporates draft, review, revision, and presentation with the same rigor as a more formal exercise. A relaxed atmosphere allows for spontaneous peer reviews as students share their work with classmates.

workflows.title: Rhymes with Relativity
workflows.description: This is for a Cegep English B-block course aimed at students in Science and 'hard' technology programs. Students usually take this in their final semester, though it can be taken earlier. In this course, students explore poetry about science and technology, reflecting upon its themes while also investigating the poetic structures. In addition, students draw on their own experiences in their field of study and create poetry that reflects the wonders, the magic, the concerns—or even the horrors—of science and technology. The second half (weeks 9-15) shows how students develop a portfolio of creative writing with analysis.

workflows.title: Social Science: Integration of Learning
workflows.description: Students will apply knowledge from the Social Science disciplines to produce a comprehensive essay on a topic that integrates at least three disciplinary perspectives. The course complements and reinforces acquired skills in the program, such as formulating a thesis, sourcing academic literature, applying academic language, and disseminating their work. Throughout the semester, students will critically engage with their learning by receiving and incorporating feedback and reflecting on their progress. The course culminates in a final paper and an oral presentation, both part of the Program Comprehensive Assessment.

workflows.title: 4 Sociological Perspectives
workflows.description:
By Cory Legassic

In this single-class activity, students explore four major sociological frameworks. Given a number of statements, they engage in a creative process to identify patterns and highlight core assumptions to group certain statements.

nodes.title: Prepare Activity
nodes.description:
• Prepare five statements related to each of the 4 perspectives
  • Place these sentences out of order into envelopes
  • Print instructions and paste on the envelope

nodes.title: Introduce Activity
nodes.description:
• Place the envelopes at each desk/work station
  • Divide the class into groups of 3-5
  • Briefly introduce the role of theoretical perspectives within the field of sociology without identifying them
  • Explain the activity instructions while students follow along with on the printed handout

nodes.title: Explore Connections
nodes.description: Identify and debate informally the similarities and connections among the different statements.

nodes.title: Group Statements by Perspective
nodes.description: Sort the statements into four groups based on what they think reflects sociological perspectives.

nodes.title: Facilitate Discussions
nodes.description: Monitor group work; visit each of the groups and affirm choices, or ask guiding questions to facilitate the activity.

nodes.title: Create Names and Logos
nodes.description: Assign a name and abstract representation (e.g. a logo) for each category.

nodes.title: Share Categories
nodes.description:
• Choose a group representative
  • Write on the smart board/poster board the way in which they chose to categorize the sentences

nodes.title: Initiate Class Discussion
nodes.description:
• Stop the activity to move to the next phase of class-wide discussion on the topic
  • Ask pointed questions to facilitate a presentation of each of the four perspectives
  • Call on groups that have identified one of the categories

nodes.title: Summarize Findings
nodes.description: In response to a prompt from the instructor, summarize group findings related to the perspective being discussed.

nodes.title: Explain Perspectives
nodes.description: Present each of the 4 theoretical perspectives, referencing the language chosen by the groups in their discussion.

workflows.title: 570-341-DW Interior Design III
workflows.description:
Last Updated from Course Framework (course description and learning outcome)

Building upon the skills and knowledge attained in Terms 1 and 2, this studio course?will introduce students to the process of designing spaces for (small scale mercantile and hospitality) commercial use, addressing?both client and end-user needs. Parameters for commercial design will be developed, formalized, and integrated into increasingly complex spaces including an introduction to building code, health, safety, welfare, and sustainability. Students will explore the process of conceptualizing, developing, and validating ideas into viable design solutions both individually and as part of a team. Materials, fixtures, furnishings, and equipment (FF&E) will be specified to meet the needs of commercial spaces. Students will learn to prepare documents that effectively explain and communicate a (the comprehensive aspects of a) design solution.
